title: Assumption Ledger
description: Per-bet assumption ledger (`bets/<bet-id>/assumptions.json` in the portfolio repo, written by scripts/assumption.py — see docs/business-factory.md §2.2, chief-wiggum#236). Discovery-driven planning's golden rule made mechanical: every assumption gets a stable id, a falsifiable XYZ-form statement, and ≥1 pre-registered test card (the ASM↔card traceability gate is check_traceability.py's shape with new node types). Status moves via `assumption.py card`/`verdict` and `bet.py transition --changed-elements` (pivot re-open, Bland's dependency rule) — never by hand; a hand-set `validated` with no supporting card verdict is a gate finding.

id.description: Stable assumption id (ASM-001…) — the node the traceability gate joins test cards against.

statement.description: The hypothesis, in Savoia's XYZ grammar: 'at least X% of Y will Z' — X numeric, Y a concrete population (not 'people'/'users'), Z a measurable behavior (not an opinion). The falsifiability linter is a parser over this field.

status.description: untested → testing at first card creation; validated|falsified from a card verdict; a pivot re-opens validated → untested for assumptions tagged to a changed canvas element.

source.description: Where the assumption was mined: a premortem (Klein — seeded defects against the plan itself), a financial-model cell, or a canvas element.

depends_on_element.description: The canvas element this assumption depends on (customer-segment, value-proposition, channel, pricing, …). Bland's dependency rule: a pivot that lists this element in --changed-elements re-opens the assumption (validated → untested) in the successor bet.

reopened_by.description: Journal record id of the pivot asm-reopen event that reset this assumption, when applicable.
